name: mac-leak
description:
REGRESSION LOCK. build_assets used to assign `mac` inside `if custom_fields:` and then only inside `if mac_info:`. Starlark locals are function-scoped, not loop-scoped, so a later row that had custom fields but no 'MAC Address' among them silently kept the PREVIOUS row's value. Hardware 13, a monitor with no MAC recorded in Snipe-IT at all, was imported carrying hardware 12's laptop MAC -- and because MAC is a matching attribute, runZero merged two unrelated assets. Every subsequent MAC-less row inherited the same address, so one populated row could pull an entire inventory onto a single asset. A row whose custom_fields lacked 'MAC Address' on the FIRST iteration reached a different abort: 'local variable mac referenced before assignment'.

The fix is `mac = None` at the top of each iteration. This scenario pins it: hardware 12 keeps its own MAC, and hardware 13 must have NO MAC and correlate on the address from its IP Address custom field instead.
